info.name: APsystems OpenAPI
info.description:
Version 1.6 | 2024-02-07

## Overview

[APsystems](https://apsystems.com) is a global leader in multi-platform module-level power electronics (MLPE) solutions for the solar PV industry. They offer a range of products including microinverters, energy storage solutions, and rapid shutdown devices.

The APsystem OpenAPI provides access to information and metrics on installed systems and underlying inverters, meters, and ECUs (Energy Communication Units).

## Pre-requisites

To call the API, you will need the system identifier along with a unique application identifier and secret key.

These values must be stored as Postman variables {{systemId}}, {{appId}}, and {{appSecret}} (see collection-level variables). For consumers, these can be obtained in the [APsystems dashboard settings ](https://apsystemsema.com/apsystems/web/setting/personalSetting/openAPIService) under OpenAPI.

Note that a collection level pre-script is used to compute the signature and set headers for each request.

## Support

For more information, refer to the [APsystems OpenAPI User Manual ](https://file.apsystemsema.com:8083/apsystems/resource/openapi/Apsystems_OpenAPI_User_Manual_End_User_EN.pdf) or contact [apisupport@apsystems.com](https://mailto:apisupport@apsystems.com).

## Response Codes

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeed to request |
| 1000 | Data exception |
| 1001 | No data |
| 2000 | Application account exception |
| 2001 | Invalid application account. |
| 2002 | The application account is not authorized. |
| 2003 | Application account authorization expires. |
| 2004 | The application account has no permission. |
| 2005 | The access limit of the application account was exceeded. |
| 3000 | Access token exception. |
| 3001 | Missing access token. |
| 3002 | Unable to verify access token. |
| 3003 | Access token timeout. |
| 3004 | Refresh token timeout. |
| 4000 | Request parameter exception. |
| 4001 | Invalid request parameter. |
| 5000 | Internal server exception. |
| 6000 | Communication exception. |
| 7000 | Server access restriction exception. |
| 7001 | Server access limit exceeded. |
| 7002 | Too many requests, please request later. |
| 7003 | The system is busy,please request later. |

exec: * APsystems OpenAPI Signature & Header Automation Pre-request Script
* This script prepares all required headers and computes the HMAC signature
* for authenticating requests to the APsystems OpenAPI in Postman.
* - Automatically generates current timestamp and a random nonce (UUID hex).
* - Resolves all variable and path parameter substitutions in the request URL,
* - Extracts the final segment of the request path for use in the signature.
* - Composes the signing string per APsystems API specification.
* - Computes the signature using HmacSHA256 and Base64 encodes it.
* - Stores all derived values (timestamp, nonce, signature) as collection variables
*   for use in your request headers.
* - Set your 'appId' and 'appSecret' as collection variables before using this script.
* - Add this script as a collection-level pre-request script for all APsystems
* - Reference the computed variables in your request headers as:
// Retrieve the required APsystems App ID and App Secret from collection variables.
// These must be set in your collection variables prior to running this script.
// Validate that both required credentials are present. If not, throw an error.
throw new Error("APsystems 'appId' and 'appSecret' collection variables must be set before making a request.");
// Generate the current timestamp in milliseconds since epoch and store as a string collection variable
// Generate a random UUID and remove dashes for the nonce, then store as a collection variable
// Retrieve the request URL as a string
// Resolve any path parameters (/:foo) and variable placeholders ({{foo}}) in the URL
// Split the resolved URL into segments and extract the last segment for the signature string
// Compose the string to sign according to APsystems API specification
// Compute the signature using HmacSHA256 and encode it in Base64
// Store the final signature as a collection variable for use in request headers

* Looks up values in path variables, then environment, collection, and globals.

* @returns {string} - The path with all parameters replaced by their resolved values.
